source.title: A0–A2: Browser-first Admin qualification, modular refactor and Integration Store UI gate
source.body:
# Admin-first browser audit and Integration Store modularization gate
**Baseline (2026-10-27):** `main` `a75e6b5ec436df25a9ac6ba82fc6b36e9e945e1d` (PR #53). This issue is design/research/qualification scope ONLY; **no code restructuring, Production write, deployment or integration activation has been made by this issue**.

## Approval and strict execution order
1. **A0 Human-observable browser walk** — one continuous, browser-driven, role-correct Admin session, starting from login; follow only links/buttons/search/forms visible in the UI. Do not use direct deep links, APIs, database calls, DevTools/JS injection, server-only shortcuts or fixture mutations to *perform this walkthrough*. Preserve video/trace/screenshot/time/commit evidence. Review environment preferred for sample form/file interactions; never pay, send mail, register domains or provision in Production. Test additional role views by normal sign-out/sign-in only.
2. **A1 Safe Admin architecture refactor** — using A0 route/call-site evidence, split feature configs and long components; create redirects only for clearly deprecated navigation after approval; remove legacy files **only after** dependency analysis + tests + verified browser parity. No API/schema/secret/payment authority changes.
3. **A2 Integration Store UI + vendor logo sourcing** — match Octalve Booking searchable provider cards and filters, use accessible per-provider side sheet. Catalogue state vs connection state separated; real vendor-specific form inputs remain unavailable until secure backend B is qualified. Logos: official source/brand rules, locally bundled verified sanitized assets, license/attribution ledger, fallback icon.
4. **B–H** credential/authority, DirectAdmin+WHM, OPanel dual-panel, registrar/DNS, mail/SSL, VPS/dedicated/data-centre and operational certification, each separate reviewed gates.

## Verified code baseline (source, not browser)
- 84 Admin page entry points, 14 Settings sections; 134 total routes x 6 viewports = 804 planned browser cases; `frontend/scripts/browser-parity-qualification.cjs` expressly says browser evidence **PENDING**.
- `frontend/src/app/admin/layout.tsx` uses `RoleGuard allowed={["admin"]}`; JS role guard does **not** replace Django enforcement.
- Current `/admin/servers/new` renders generic `AdminResourceEditorView`, with generic provider `base_url/username/api_key/secret/status` fields in `features/admin/data/admin-editor-config.ts`.
- `AdminResourceEditorView.tsx` ~335 lines; `CatalogAuthorityWorkbench.tsx` ~256 lines /22KB; `admin-workspace-config.ts` ~292 lines. They combine concerns and should be split by domain while preserving semantics.
- Main installed Django provider app: `backend/providers/` (`providers.apps.ProvidersConfig`). There is also `backend/apps/providers/` with a separate adapter registry; **audit imports before deleting or consolidating**. Existing `payments`, `domains`, `catalog`, `provisioning`, and independent `octalve-opanel` retain business authority.
- `octalve-booking` `components/booking/WorkspaceViews.tsx` provides searchable integration grid/card filters; its integration POST endpoint is presently disabled and **not** reusable as a live credential service.
- OPanel vendor read-back supports guarded DirectAdmin/WHM lookup; unrestricted technical writes and dual-panel management are not yet qualified.

## A0: one continuous click-path protocol (strictly no deep-link jumps)
- Open public Console address > use visible Log in > authenticate by form > reach Admin Overview; record visible version/URL + role.
- Navigate all **visible Admin sidebar categories** in order: Command (Overview, Customers, Staff); Commerce (Category, Products, Plans, Orders, Invoices, Transactions); Infrastructure (Services, Domains, Gateways, Providers, Provisioning); Operations (Support, Knowledge Base, Rewards, Reports, Audit Logs, Route Audit, Settings).
- For each destination, use on-page search, filter, sort and pagination if visibly offered; open a record by clicking its row, use visible Back/breadcrumb to return; note broken links, loading states, unqualified Save actions, spacing, accessibility, real/placeholder data, and role errors. Never fabricate fixture record IDs.
- In Settings, open all 14 sections **by selecting cards** from hub, navigate actual related links and return through UI. Verify Providers opens real hosting records, Gateways separate payment records, domain records separate from registrar, Catalogue separate retail pricing. Record ambiguous duplicated destinations.
- In Providers, click Add provider (do not submit real credentials); observe dropdown options and how model/status is presented; test blank/invalid *local* form validation only in isolated Review, no server mutations. For any available logo upload in Review, select a harmless local sample through the file picker, only if feature is visibly offered; otherwise mark not available.
- Follow user-accessible navigation to invoice designer, catalogue workbench, support and approval workflows. Never mark a paid invoice, purchase domain, send email, or execute remote provisioning.
- Test responsive UI and focus/keyboard Escape/Tab/Shift+Tab on a separate browser-led pass while keeping the same navigational flow; test mobile width via browser viewport rather than altering application code.
- Finish via visible Logout. Other roles: repeat by ordinary login with authorized test accounts in isolated Review only. **No skip to /admin/... paths via URL bar except the initial public site/login address.**
- Collect evidence: ordered click ledger, browser screenshots/trace, failing action, URL after click, reproducibility, release SHA, environment, account role, viewport. Tests based solely on source inspection cannot pass A0.

## Proposed route ownership (preserve stable URLs until A0 passes)
- `/admin` remains dashboard.
- `/admin/settings` remains Settings; existing `/admin/settings/providers` becomes discovery link to **Integrations** without new independent secrets.
- `/admin/servers` remains legacy provider record route until integration migration qualifies; never blindly remove existing records or endpoints.
- Proposed `/admin/integrations` as store (after A0/A1); `/admin/integrations/connections` as installed/authorized connections. Sheets are URL-addressable only if a real user can reach through store cards; guard deep-route reload.
- `/admin/gateways` preserves payment/financial authority; `/admin/catalog/workbench` preserves retail pricing; OPanel remains independent repo.

## Proposed modular frontend tree (A1/A2 target, NOT yet created)
```
frontend/src/app/admin/                # thin route entry points, auth layout
frontend/src/features/admin/
  overview/
  customers/
  staff/
  commerce/{catalog,orders,invoices,transactions,billing}/
  infrastructure/{services,domains,provisioning}/
  integrations/
    catalog/{manifests,categories,search}/
    connections/{list,details,status}/
    sheets/{IntegrationSheet,Requirements,Configuration,Verification}/
    adapters/{hosting,registrars,dns,ssl,mail,payments,cloud,vps}/
    assets/{sources,usage-ledger}/
    shared/{types,components,validation}/
  operations/{support,knowledge,reports,audit}/
  settings/
  shared/{components,hooks,types,api}/
```
Keep feature modules cohesive and typically <=200–250 lines, with thin route adapters. Do not split a 30-line cohesive component solely to inflate file count. Preserve existing shared `features/shell` and design-system; do not copy shell, pricing, payments, or entitlement logic. Adapter manifests are **server-authored/versioned**; TS UI may only render approved fields, never define outbound authority.

## Detailed refactor acceptance gates
- Before changes: capture all existing link destinations, API operations, permissions and baseline CI. Classify duplicate pages as redirect / reuse / retained / safe to retire; no unverified deletion.
- After each narrowly scoped PR: exact SHA TypeScript/Next build, Django/security, source-to-route and owner scopes, financial write guard, provider adapter security and browser visual parity on representative workflows.
- A1 no business write behaviour changes; same API paths, same customer session, same invoice/payment rules, same provider records, OPanel SSO unchanged; no new migrations.
- Store logo sourcing: prefer official vendor press/brand-kit SVG/PNG, original aspect/color, no implied partnership; security-sanitize SVG or use approved raster, local immutable filenames, record brand usage restrictions and documentation URLs.
- A2 side sheet: desktop right panel and mobile full-screen sheet, focus trap, accessible name, Escape close, background inert, close-button, return focus, unsaved-change confirmation, responsive scroll. Vendor-level availability distinct from specific connection state.
- B secrets only after backend has deny-by-default role checks, isolated encryption/rotation, SSRF protection and immutable audit. Store UI cannot make an adapter executable.
- Do **not** use screenshots, demos or signed manifests alone as evidence of successful authenticated browser interaction; signoff must attest real browser behavior.
- Production deploy and alias health remain separate from green GitHub CI; Vercel build-rate limit currently unresolved.

## Reference standards
- Next.js App Router intercepting/parallel routes: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/intercepting-routes
- W3C dialog modal keyboard/focus: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/
- Playwright authenticated browser use and sensitive cookies: https://playwright.dev/docs/auth
- OWASP Web Security Testing Guide: https://owasp.org/projects/web-security-testing-guide
- OWASP Secrets Management: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html
- Vendor logos: https://www.directadmin.com/extras-logos.php ; https://www.cpanel.net/company/cpanel-brand-guide/
